entries.name: Accuracy
entries.definition: Share of all predictions or judgements that match the reference label.
entries.usage_note: Misleading when classes are imbalanced; report alongside class-wise metrics.
entries.example: classification accuracy on the held-out test set

entries.name: Precision
entries.definition: Share of items labelled positive that are truly positive.
entries.example: precision of the extracted phrase candidates

entries.name: Recall
entries.definition: Share of truly positive items that the procedure labels positive.
entries.example: recall against the annotated reference set

entries.name: F1 score
entries.definition: Harmonic mean of precision and recall, giving both equal weight.
entries.usage_note: State whether it is macro-, micro- or weighted-averaged across classes.
entries.example: macro-averaged F1 score

entries.name: Cohen's kappa
entries.definition: Agreement between two raters on categorical labels, corrected for agreement expected by chance.
entries.usage_note: Use for exactly two raters; report the number of items rated.
entries.example: inter-rater agreement measured with Cohen's kappa

entries.name: Cronbach's alpha
entries.definition: Internal consistency of a set of items intended to measure the same construct.
entries.usage_note: Report per subscale, not only for the whole questionnaire.
entries.example: internal consistency of the satisfaction subscale

entries.name: Root mean square error
entries.definition: Square root of the mean squared difference between predicted and observed values, in the outcome's unit.
entries.example: prediction error expressed as RMSE in minutes

entries.name: Mean score
entries.definition: Arithmetic mean of item or scale scores across respondents.
entries.usage_note: Report with a spread measure such as the standard deviation.
entries.example: mean satisfaction score (M) with standard deviation (SD)

entries.name: Cohen's d
entries.definition: Difference between two group means divided by a pooled standard deviation.
entries.example: the size of the difference between groups, expressed as Cohen's d

entries.name: Response rate
entries.definition: Share of invited participants who returned a usable response.
entries.example: a response rate of the invited sample

entries.name: 5-point Likert scale questionnaire
entries.definition: Respondents rate agreement with statements on five ordered options, usually from strongly disagree to strongly agree.
entries.usage_note: Ordinal data; state how items were combined into scale scores.
entries.example: a questionnaire rated on a five-point Likert scale

entries.name: 7-point Likert scale questionnaire
entries.definition: Respondents rate agreement on seven ordered options, giving finer gradation than five points.
entries.example: items rated on a seven-point scale

entries.name: Semi-structured interview
entries.definition: Interview that follows a prepared guide of open questions while allowing follow-up questions.
entries.usage_note: Describe the guide, duration and how responses were recorded and coded.
entries.example: semi-structured interviews with course instructors

entries.name: Expert annotation
entries.definition: Trained annotators assign labels to items using a written guideline.
entries.usage_note: Report annotator training, guideline version and agreement.
entries.example: manual annotation by two trained linguists

entries.name: Timed task
entries.definition: Participants complete a defined task while the time to completion is recorded.
entries.example: a timed usability task

entries.name: A/B test
entries.definition: Users are assigned at random to two variants and an outcome is compared between them.
entries.example: an A/B test of two recommendation layouts

entries.name: Held-out evaluation
entries.definition: A model or procedure is scored on data that was not used to build or tune it.
entries.example: evaluation on a held-out test split

entries.name: Pre-test/post-test design
entries.definition: The same measure is applied before and after an intervention to estimate change.
entries.usage_note: Without a control group, change cannot be attributed to the intervention alone.
entries.example: a pre-test/post-test design with a comparison group

entries.name: Randomised assignment
entries.definition: Participants are allocated to conditions by a random procedure so groups are comparable on average.
entries.example: participants were randomly assigned to two conditions

entries.name: Standardised data collection
entries.definition: Every participant is measured with the same instructions, materials, order and setting.
entries.usage_note: Report the instructions and setting so the procedure can be repeated.
entries.example: data were collected from all participants following the same procedure

entries.name: Double annotation with adjudication
entries.definition: Two annotators label each item independently; disagreements are resolved by a third reviewer.
entries.example: each item was labelled by two annotators and disagreements were adjudicated

entries.name: Train/development/test split
entries.definition: Data are divided before modelling into separate sets for fitting, tuning and final scoring.
entries.usage_note: Split by document or group when items from one source are correlated.
entries.example: an article-level split into training, development and test sets

entries.name: Significance level
entries.definition: Threshold probability below which a test result is treated as statistically significant, fixed before the analysis.
entries.usage_note: State the threshold and whether tests were one- or two-sided; report exact p values where possible.
entries.example: a significance level of 0.05 (two-sided)

entries.name: Independent-samples t-test
entries.definition: Compares the means of one continuous outcome between two unrelated groups.
entries.usage_note: Report group means, standard deviations, the t statistic, degrees of freedom and an effect size.
entries.example: an independent-samples t-test comparing the two groups

entries.name: Non-parametric test
entries.definition: Hypothesis test that does not assume a particular distribution, usually working on ranks.
entries.usage_note: Name the specific test and say why a parametric test was not used.
entries.example: a Mann-Whitney U test, because the scores were not normally distributed

entries.name: Descriptive statistics
entries.definition: Summaries of the collected data, such as counts, means, medians and spreads, before any inferential test.
entries.example: descriptive statistics for all variables
